items.title: Remove the test:autopilot-resume-smoke script entry from packages/main/package.json
items.context: Line 70: "test:autopilot-resume-smoke": "node dist/tasks/autopilot-resume-smoke.js" — source deleted in 5d3d7bd686; root package.json has no mirror of this script

happy.desc: After removing the script line, run `node -e "const p=require(./packages/main/package.json); if(p.scripts[\"test:autopilot-resume-smoke\"]) { process.exit(1) }"` -> exits 0, confirming the key is absent from the parsed scripts object; WHY: proves the script entry was actually removed, not just commented out
Run `npm --prefix packages/main run` and pipe through grep for autopilot-resume-smoke -> no match (exit 1 from grep); WHY: confirms npm no longer lists the script as runnable
Run `node -e "require(./packages/main/package.json)"` -> exits 0 with no parse error; WHY: validates JSON is still well-formed after the line deletion (no dangling comma)

edge.desc: Inspect the line before and after the deleted line 70 in the committed diff to confirm no trailing comma was left on the now-last script entry and no blank line gap was introduced -> diff shows clean removal; WHY: a dangling comma makes package.json invalid JSON in strict parsers and npm versions that reject trailing commas

Run `node -e "const p=require(./packages/main/package.json); const keys=Object.keys(p.scripts); if(keys.length===0) process.exit(1)"` -> exits 0; WHY: guard against accidentally deleting the entire scripts block or adjacent entries during the edit

adversarial.desc: Verify that running `npm --prefix packages/main run test:autopilot-resume-smoke` after the removal produces an npm error (missing script), NOT a MODULE_NOT_FOUND from node -> npm error output contains missing script or not found; WHY: confirms the failure mode shifted from a confusing node module error to a clear npm missing-script error, proving the entry was removed rather than the dist artifact being cleaned

Check that no other scripts key in packages/main/package.json contains the substring autopilot-resume-smoke (e.g. as a dependency in a compound script like npm run test:autopilot-resume-smoke &&...) -> grep of the scripts block returns no match; WHY: ensures no transitive reference that would still fail at runtime

items.title: Verify no remaining runnable reference to autopilot-resume-smoke outside historical story artifacts and decision-doc evidence records
items.context: grep the repo excluding .lattice story artifacts, .claude/worktrees and node_modules; docs/requirements/decisions/autopilot-v2-reliability-execution-plan.md:403 is a historical B-320f evidence row and stays untouched

happy.desc: Run `grep -rn autopilot-resume-smoke . --include="*.json" --include="*.ts" --include="*.js" --include="*.yml" --include="*.yaml" --include="*.sh" --include="*.md" --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=dist --exclude-dir=.worktrees --exclude-dir=.claude` and filter out .lattice/story lines -> only surviving hit is docs/requirements/decisions/autopilot-v2-reliability-execution-plan.md:403; WHY: confirms no runnable reference (npm script, CI config, shell script, smoke manifest) remains after CHK-001

Verify the surviving hit at docs/requirements/decisions/autopilot-v2-reliability-execution-plan.md:403 is a historical evidence table row (contains B-320f and is inside a markdown table) and is NOT a runnable invocation -> line content is a pipe-delimited table row mentioning B-320f; WHY: confirms the only remaining mention is a historical record, not an active command

edge.desc: Run the grep without file-type filters (all files) to catch references in unexpected file types like Makefile, Dockerfile, or .env files -> no additional runnable hits beyond the known decision-doc row; WHY: file-type-filtered grep can miss references in non-standard file types that could still be executed

Search specifically in root package.json for autopilot-resume-smoke -> no match; WHY: the plan notes root package.json has no mirror but this should be independently verified, not trusted from the plan description alone

Check that .lattice/story/actives/ may contain references in closed-story artifacts and that these are correctly excluded from the runnable-reference scope -> any hits in .lattice/story are story metadata, not runnable scripts; WHY: prevents false positives from story artifacts being flagged as missed cleanup

adversarial.desc: Search for partial-match variants that could hide a reference: grep for resume-smoke (without the autopilot- prefix) across runnable file types excluding the known exclusion dirs -> no unexpected hits that reference the deleted smoke under a different prefix or alias; WHY: catches cases where the script was referenced by a shortened name or where a wrapper script uses a substring match

Verify that no npm lifecycle hook (pretest, posttest, prepare, etc.) in packages/main/package.json invokes test:autopilot-resume-smoke indirectly via npm run -> inspect all lifecycle-hook script values for the substring; WHY: npm lifecycle hooks execute implicitly and a hidden reference would cause silent failures during npm install/test/publish

Check that the decision-doc line at :403 was NOT modified by this story (git diff of that file shows no changes) -> diff is empty for that file; WHY: scope contract explicitly excludes this file; any edit would violate the scope boundary and corrupt historical evidence
